title: TracePoint run configuration
description: A TracePoint load test. Written as YAML or JSON. At least one runner section (http, db, redis) must be present. Storage runners double as probes: their latency is a direct health signal for that tier while the app is under load. Unknown keys are rejected with a suggestion.

duration.description: A Go duration string: a number and a unit, optionally repeated. Units: ns, us, ms, s, m, h.

templateString.description: A string that may contain template tokens: {{var}} from an earlier step's extract, {{feedername.column}} from a CSV feeder, or a generator - randInt a b, randString n, uuid, seq, pick a|b|c, now. ${ENV} and ${ENV:-default} are interpolated at load time, before templating.

run.description: Timing and determinism for the whole run. One monotonic clock is shared by every runner and sampler.

name.description: Human label for the run, shown in reports and stored in the run directory.

duration.description: Total load duration, excluding graceful drain. Executor stages, when given, must sum to this.

bucket.description: Width of the shared time bucket every layer is recorded into. Smaller buckets localise incidents better but need more traffic to stay above min_samples.

warmup.description: Leading period excluded from summaries, baselines and SLO evaluation. Shaded in charts. Use it to let pools fill and caches warm.

grace.description: How long to let in-flight work drain after arrivals stop before the context is cancelled.

timeout.description: Default per-operation timeout for every runner. Individual requests, queries and commands may override it. Also sets how long a bucket waits before sealing.

seed.description: Seed for every random choice: weighted picks, generators and Poisson arrivals. Recorded in result.json so a run can be reproduced. Omit to draw one and record it.

arrival.description: Arrival process for open-model executors. uniform spaces arrivals evenly along the rate profile; poisson draws exponential gaps with the same mean, which is a better model of independent users and produces natural bursts.

min_samples.description: Buckets with fewer than this many completed operations are marked insufficient: they are displayed but never used as evidence for a hot bucket, an incident or a verdict.

tags.description: Free-form key/value labels copied into result.json - useful for correlating runs with commits, environments or tickets.

sloTarget.description: Latency and error budgets for one runner. Evaluated on response_time (what a user feels), not service_time. A breach makes the run exit 1.

p99.description: 99th percentile response time budget. Also the default hot-bucket threshold for this runner.

error_rate.description: Maximum share of operations that may fail.

slo.description: Per-runner service level objectives. Keys are runner names: http, db, redis.

safety.description: Limits this configuration accepts. Safety can only tighten the human-granted policy (--policy, TRACEPOINT_POLICY); it can never widen it. A value looser than policy is a refusal, not a warning.

allow_writes.description: Permit SQL statements and Redis commands classified as writes. Without it, writes are refused at load time.

allow_dangerous.description: Permit destructive or administrative statements (DROP, TRUNCATE, ALTER, FLUSHALL, FLUSHDB, SHUTDOWN, CONFIG SET, DEBUG, SCRIPT FLUSH). Almost never correct against a shared database.

allow_targets.description: Hosts, IPs or CIDRs that may be targeted even though they are public. Loopback, private and link-local addresses are always allowed. Public targets not listed here are refused with exit 2.

allow_insecure_tls.description: Permit tls.insecure_skip_verify. When used, every report says so.

max_rate_per_runner.description: Ceiling on offered operations per second for any single runner.

max_in_flight.description: Ceiling on concurrent in-flight operations for any single runner.

abortGuard.description: Stops the run early when the target is clearly failing, so a broken deployment is not hammered. Connection errors, timeouts and 5xx count; 4xx and 429 do not.

error_ratio.description: Failure share that trips the guard.

window.description: How long the ratio must hold before aborting.

stage.description: One segment of a load profile. The value ramps linearly from the previous stage's target (or from 0 at the start) to this target over this duration; equal targets hold flat.

target.description: Value reached at the end of the segment: operations per second for arrival-rate, virtual users for vus.

executor.description: How work is generated. arrival-rate is the open model: arrivals fire on a schedule regardless of whether the target keeps up, which is what makes latency coordinated-omission correct. vus is the closed model: a fixed population of virtual users each loop as fast as the target allows, which throttles itself when the target slows. An executor must say how much load to offer: a rate, a vu count, or a stage profile. There is no sensible default for that, so omitting all three is an error rather than a silent choice.

type.description: Executor model. Use arrival-rate to measure how a system behaves at a load level; use vus to model a bounded user population.

rate.description: Shorthand for a single constant arrival-rate stage lasting run.duration. Mutually exclusive with stages.

vus.description: Shorthand for a single constant vus stage lasting run.duration. Mutually exclusive with stages.

stages.description: Piecewise-linear profile. Stage durations must sum to run.duration.

max_in_flight.description: Worker ceiling for arrival-rate. When every worker is busy and the dispatch queue is full, the arrival is dropped and counted rather than delayed without bound. Little's Law sizes it: rate x p99 service time.

queue_depth.description: Depth of the bounded dispatch queue in front of the workers. Absorbs brief bursts without hiding sustained overload.

pick.description: For vus: whether each virtual user re-picks a weighted request or journey every iteration, or is pinned to one for the whole run.

expect.description: What a successful response looks like. A response that fails an expectation is recorded as an error and, in a journey, stops the iteration.

status.description: Acceptable status codes. Defaults to any 2xx or 3xx.

json.description: Assertions against the JSON body, evaluated with gjson paths.

path.description: gjson path into the response body.

exists.description: Require the path to be present.

equals.description: Require the value at the path to equal this, compared as JSON.

max_body_bytes.description: Fail the response if the body exceeds this size. Bodies are read and discarded, never stored.

extract.description: Values pulled out of a response and made available to later steps in the same journey as {{name}}. If an extraction fails at runtime the step fails with extract_failed and the iteration stops - a literal {{token}} is never sent.

name.description: Variable name later steps reference as {{name}}.

path.description: A gjson path when from is body, a header name when from is header, ignored when from is status.

thinkTime.description: Pause after a step, modelling a user reading the page. Think time is excluded from journey duration and from every latency statistic.

httpStep.description: One HTTP call. A top-level request is a single-step journey; inside a journey, steps run in order and share extracted variables and a cookie jar.

name.description: Label for this call. Labels group statistics; keep them stable and low-cardinality - never put an id in a name.

weight.description: Relative probability of being picked, among top-level requests or journeys. Ignored on journey steps.

url.description: Absolute URL, or a path when http.base_url is set.

headers.description: Per-call headers, merged over http.headers. Authorization and Cookie values are redacted from every artifact.

body.description: Request body. Mutually exclusive with body_file.

body_file.description: Path to a file used as the request body, read once at load time. Mutually exclusive with body.

feeder.description: A CSV file supplying parameter data. Columns are referenced as {{feedername.column}}.

name.description: Feeder name used in template tokens.

file.description: Path to a CSV file with a header row.

mode.description: How rows are handed out: sequential cycles in order, random samples with replacement, unique gives every iteration a distinct row and fails when the file is exhausted.

insecure_skip_verify.description: Skip certificate verification. Requires safety.allow_insecure_tls, marks the run degraded and is printed in every report.

http.description: The application tier: the traffic whose latency users actually feel. Provide either requests (each becomes a single-step journey) or journeys, never both.

base_url.description: Prefix for step URLs that are written as paths.

headers.description: Headers added to every request, overridable per step.

traceparent.description: Inject a W3C traceparent header so an APM can join TracePoint traffic to its own traces.

transport.description: Connection behaviour. Defaults are sized from the executor so the client is not the bottleneck.

max_idle_conns_per_host.description: Idle connection pool per host. Defaults to max_in_flight so keep-alive actually holds.

keep_alive.description: Reuse connections. Turning this off measures connection setup on every request.

feeders.description: CSV data sources for this runner.

requests.description: Weighted single calls. Sugar for one-step journeys.

steps.description: Ordered steps. Each step may use variables extracted by earlier steps.

db.description: The SQL tier. This runner is both load and probe: it queries the database directly, so its latency is a direct health signal for the database while the application is under load.

driver.description: Database driver. Aliases such as postgresql and psql normalise to postgres.

dsn.description: Connection string. Use ${ENV} - passwords are redacted from every artifact.

pool.description: Connection pool. Connections are acquired explicitly so pool wait is timed apart from query time.

max_open.description: Maximum open connections. Defaults to the executor's worker count. A warning is raised when this exceeds the server's max_connections.

max_idle.description: Maximum idle connections. Defaults to max_open so connections are not churned.

conn_max_lifetime.description: Maximum age of a connection before it is retired.

conn_max_idle_time.description: Maximum idle time before a connection is retired.

tag_sessions.description: Set application_name to tracepoint/<run-id> (Postgres) so test traffic is identifiable in pg_stat_activity.

comment_queries.description: Prefix each statement with a sqlcommenter-style comment carrying the run id and label, so slow logs and pg_stat_statements can attribute test traffic.

queries.description: Weighted statements. Each item is either a single sql statement or a tx unit of statements run in one transaction.

type.description: Read or write. Authoritative: it overrides the statement-text heuristic and drives the write guard.

sql.description: A single statement. Mutually exclusive with tx.

args.description: Bind arguments, in order. An argument that is exactly one generator keeps its native type, so {{randInt 1 100}} binds as an integer.

tx.description: Statements executed in one transaction and timed as one unit. Mutually exclusive with sql.

prepare.description: Use a prepared statement. Preflight prepares every statement regardless, to catch typos without executing them.

redis.description: The cache tier. Like db, this runner is both load and probe.

addr.description: host:port for mode single. Mutually exclusive with addrs.

addrs.description: Node addresses for cluster or sentinel. Mutually exclusive with addr.

master_name.description: Sentinel master name, required for mode sentinel.

password.description: Password. Use ${ENV}; it is redacted from every artifact.

db.description: Logical database index. Not valid for cluster mode.

pool.description: Connection pool. Sized at or above the worker count so pool wait does not masquerade as Redis latency.

size.description: Connections per node. Defaults to the executor's worker count.

commands.description: Weighted commands, each an argument array.

type.description: Read or write, overriding the classification derived from the command name.

cmd.description: Command and arguments. Mutually exclusive with pipeline.

pipeline.description: Several commands sent in one round trip and timed as one unit. Mutually exclusive with cmd.

samplerToggle.description: Either a boolean to enable a sampler with its defaults, or an object to configure it.

dsn.description: Separate read-only connection string for sampling. Defaults to the runner's DSN.

statements.description: Postgres only: collect a top-N snapshot from pg_stat_statements at the end of the run.

latency.description: Redis only: read LATENCY LATEST, when the latency monitor is enabled on the server.

telemetry.description: Server-side health sampled on the same clock as the load, used to corroborate a verdict. Every sampler is read-only, uses one dedicated connection and fails soft: a missing permission degrades to 'unavailable: <reason>' rather than failing the run. Generator self-health is always collected.

capacity.description: Turns the run into an auto-ramp capacity search: levels are tried until one breaks an SLO or plateaus, then the boundary is refined and confirmed.

runner.description: Which runner the knob applies to.

max.description: Ceiling; the search stops here even if nothing has broken.

step_duration.description: Length of each level, including the settle period.

settle.description: Leading part of each level discarded before measuring. Defaults to 20% of step_duration.

cooldown.description: Idle gap between levels. Connections stay warm.

refine.description: How to search between the last ok level and the first broken one: bisection, or linear:N for N evenly spaced levels.

resolution.description: Stop refining once the gap between last-ok and first-broken is at or below this. Defaults to max(1, 5% of the broken level).

confirm.description: Re-run the boundary levels once; if either flips, report an unstable range instead of a point.
